featured_reviews.name: Anil Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
My overall experience with the medical team and flight crew was positive. Both doctors were professional and caring throughout the transfer. Dr. Baig was particularly dynamic, attentive, and reassuring, helping to instill confidence during a stressful situation. Dr. Yadav was also supportive, competent, and compassionate. The pilot and co-pilot performed their duties excellently, and we felt safe throughout the journey.
The most important outcome was that the patient was transported safely and received continuous medical attention during the flight. For this, the doctors and flight crew deserve sincere appreciation.
However, regarding the aircraft itself, I would hesitate to describe it as a fully equipped ICU air ambulance. The cabin appeared somewhat cluttered and unorganized, making movement and working conditions less comfortable than expected. There was no visible inbuilt oxygen system, and certain ICU-related facilities seemed to be unavailable, requiring the medical team to manually manage and change equipment during the journey.
In general, a true ICU air ambulance is expected to function as a flying intensive care unit, equipped with features such as an inbuilt oxygen system with adequate backup supply, ventilator support, multi-parameter monitoring, infusion pumps, suction equipment, organized storage, sufficient working space around the patient, and dedicated power backup for medical devices. While the medical team handled the situation efficiently and professionally, the aircraft infrastructure appeared to fall short of these expectations.
I would also like to comment on the cost. Considering the facilities and infrastructure available on board, the charge of approximately ₹18 lakhs appeared relatively high. I fully appreciate that air ambulance operations involve substantial expenses, including aircraft operation, medical personnel, logistics, and emergency readiness. Nevertheless, the level of onboard equipment and infrastructure did not seem entirely commensurate with the amount charged.
My intention is not to criticize the doctors or flight crew, who were excellent in every respect, but rather to provide honest and constructive feedback regarding the aircraft infrastructure and overall value for money. It may be worthwhile for the management to review the equipment standards, cabin organization, and pricing structure so that the service can better meet the expectations associated with a fully equipped ICU air ambulance.
Overall, I remain grateful to Dr. Baig, Dr. Yadav, and the flight crew for their professionalism, dedication, and care. The patient was transported safely, which remains the most important outcome, though there is certainly scope for improvement in the aircraft's medical infrastructure and organization.
